originalTitle: Water supply restored to Gatwick airport after hours without working toilets
summary: Airport’s bars and restaurants were also unable to serve drinks to passengers because of lack of running water
content: Water supply has been restored to most of Gatwick airport after passengers spent hours without access to working toilets, and bars and restaurants were closed. Most toilets had reopened across both terminals on Sunday evening, with the remaining facilities, including bars and restaurants, expected to return to normal for the first of Monday’s flights. Although flights were unaffected, toilets in both terminals were out of use, cafes, restaurants and bars were shut, and taps were either not running at all or running with low pressure since Sunday morning. Announcing that the water, supplied by SES Water, had been restored, Gatwick airport said: “Following an issue at the Bough Beech water treatment works which impacted the local area today, we are pleased to report that the water supply has now returned to the vast majority of the London Gatwick campus. “Most toilet facilities are now open and we expect all toilets – as well as food and beverage outlets – to be open for tomorrow’s first flights. Since becoming aware of the issue, we have been working closely with @SESWater and our airport partners to help minimise the impact, and ensure all today’s flights departed as scheduled.” Earlier on Sunday, passengers posted online that they were unable to get hot drinks, wash their hands or fill water bottles at the airport in Sussex. The problem also had an impact in the wider Sussex and Kent area, water suppliers said. SES Water said there had been interruptions to water supplies in parts of the TN11, RH1, RH6 and RH10 postcode areas. At 2pm the company had said its Bough Beech water treatment works were running again but the water needed to be treated before services could return to normal. On Facebook, one user posted: “Gasping for a drink & crossing my legs right now. This is ridiculous! Gatwick airport has shut all restaurants and most toilets due to a water outage. Not a great start to the holiday.” The former MP and recently appointed government “music champion” Michael Dugher wrote on social media: “At least allow people to use the chairs in all the closed restaurants and bars. No water is one thing, but depriving people of somewhere to sit is another … Families are having to sit on the floor.” Roger Wood, from Tunbridge Wells, Kent, arrived at Gatwick’s south terminal at about 11am on Sunday to fly to New York. He told reporters: “There was no communication. We arrived at 11ish and it had only started recently. “We met friends at the bar but they couldn’t serve us as they were unable to wash their hands. I’ve never seen Wetherspoons empty. No idea when it’ll be resolved. The toilets also lacked water to wash hands.”
chineseTitle: 盖特威克机场下班后恢复供水，但厕所无法使用
chineseSummary: 由于缺乏自来水，机场的酒吧和餐馆也无法为乘客提供饮料
chineseContent: 在乘客数小时无法使用可用厕所后，盖特威克机场大部分地区的供水已恢复，酒吧和餐馆也已关闭。周日晚上，两个航站楼的大多数厕所已重新开放，包括酒吧和餐馆在内的其余设施预计将在周一的首个航班恢复正常。尽管航班未受到影响，但两个航站楼的厕所都已停止使用，咖啡馆、餐馆和酒吧都关闭了，自周日早上以来，水龙头要么根本不运行，要么以低压运行。盖特威克机场宣布由 SES Water 提供的供水已恢复，并表示：“继 Bough Beech 水处理厂今天出现影响当地地区的问题后，我们很高兴地报告，伦敦盖特威克机场绝大多数区域现已恢复供水。大多数厕所设施现已开放，我们预计所有厕所以及食品和饮料店都将为明天的第一批航班开放。”自从意识到这个问题以来，我们一直与@SESWater 和我们的机场合作伙伴密切合作，以帮助最大程度地减少影响，并确保今天所有航班均按计划起飞。”周日早些时候，乘客在网上发帖称，他们在苏塞克斯机场无法获得热饮、洗手或装水瓶。供水商表示，这个问题还对更广泛的苏塞克斯和肯特地区产生了影响。 SES Water表示，TN11、RH1、RH6和RH10邮政编码地区的部分地区供水中断。下午 2 点，该公司表示，其 Bough Beech 水处理厂已恢复运行，但水需要经过处理才能恢复正常。在 Facebook 上，一位用户发帖称：“现在正想喝一杯，交叉双腿。这
